contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: vectors.distance IN {Cosine, Euclid, Dot, Manhattan}; VectorParams.required = [size, distance]; vectors.size is an unsigned integer (uint64)
contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check, wrong-citation fork: the quoted clauses govern the INNER fields of a vectors config when one is present, and all of them are enforced by the API (live: vectors={"size":4} without distance -> 400). The observed phenomenon — the whole vectors object omitted — lies outside the quote's domain: no clause of the quote asserts that vectors itself must be present. The 'required=true' premise in the claim traces to the mining-layer registry row (raw_knowledge.json api_endpoints[collections+create].parameters.vectors.required=true, mirrored in structured_contract.json), which the version-pinned served OpenAPI contradicts (CreateCollection has no required array). The citation that would govern this phenomenon is a 'create must define at least one vector space' constraint, which the v1.18.x documentation does not assert (it documents vectors optional and documents PUT /collections/{name}/vectors/{vector_name} for post-create addition).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: PUT /collections/{name} -> CreateCollection serde payload: #[serde(default)] on vectors: VectorsConfig means an omitted key deserializes to VectorsConfig::default() = Multi(BTreeMap::new()) (types.rs L1475-1479); explicit vectors={} reaches the same state via the untagged-enum map variant. CreateCollectionOperation::new (collection_meta_ops.rs L192-250) validates only vector NAMES of entries that exist plus dense/sparse name uniqueness — no check that at least one vector space is defined. TableOfContent::create_collection (toc/create_collection.rs L20-147) passes vectors untouched into CollectionParams (L132-134) and persists; live readback confirms config.params.vectors = {}. Inner-field enforcement is real and separate: VectorParams{size: NonZeroU64 with custom range validator 1..=65536, distance: Distance} have no serde defaults (types.rs L1338-1343), so a partial VectorParams fails untagged deserialization -> HTTP 400 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum VectorsConfig' (live c2 + boundary_001 log L6/L8). gRPC face mirrors REST: CreateCollection.vectors_config is Option<VectorsConfig> (grpc/qdrant.rs L1196-1199).
source_grounding.by_design_evidence: explicit intent evidence: (1) maintainer comment in CreateCollectionOperation::new names 'both creation paths' for vector configs — create-time and the POST-CREATE endpoint PUT /collections/{name}/vectors/{vector_name}, whose served doc reads 'Create a new named vector on an existing collection' (openapi-collections.ytt.yaml L234-240) and whose VectorNameConfig docstring says storage/index/quantization 'can be configured separately later'; (2) the served v1.18.0 OpenAPI (docs/redoc/master/openapi.json, the artifact published to api.qdrant.tech per tools/generate_openapi_models.sh) documents vectors as optional — CreateCollection has no required array — while marking VectorParams.required=[distance,size]; (3) deliberate code: #[serde(default)] on the vectors field plus impl Default for VectorsConfig = Multi(empty) plus an explicit VectorsConfig::empty() constructor; (4) the documented sparse-only use case (sparse_vectors without dense vectors) is live-accepted (c4); (5) the shell-then-fill workflow was verified live end-to-end: create with {} -> 200, PUT /collections/{name}/vectors/myvec {"dense":{size,distance}} -> 200 acknowledged, readback config.params.vectors = {"myvec":{"size":4,"distance":"Cosine"}}. The acceptance of a vectors-less create is a designed capability, not an oversight.
